sys_hub_flow.description:
Creates a model response.

Inputs:

  • Model - Model ID used to generate the response.
  • Input - Text, image, or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response.
  • Include - Specify additional output data to include in the model response.
  • Instructions - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
  • Max Output Tokens - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
  • Metadata - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
  • Parallel Tool Calls - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
  • Previous Response ID - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
  • Reasoning - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
    • Effort - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high.
    • Generate Summary - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.
  • Store - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API.
  • Temperature - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
  • Top P - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
  • Send JSON Response - Set to true to enable JSON mode.
  • Response Format - Configuration options for a response from the model as a structured JSON data.
  • Tool Choice - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
  • Tools - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
  • Truncation - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
  • User - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse.

Outputs:

  • Output - An array of content items generated by the model.
  • ID - Unique Id for this response.
  • Object - Details of the API used for the request.
  • Created At - Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when this Response was created.
  • Model - Details of the model used for the request.
  • Status - The status of the response generation. One of completed, failed, in_progress, or incomplete.
  • Incomplete Details - Details about why the response is incomplete.
  • Instructions - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
  • Max Output Tokens - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
  • Metadata - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
  • Parallel Tool Calls - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
  • Previous Response ID - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
  • Reasoning - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
    • Effort - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high.
    • Generate Summary - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.
  • Store - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API.
  • Temperature - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
  • Top P - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
  • Text - Configuration options for a text response from the model. Can be plain text or structured JSON data.
  • Tool Choice - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
  • Tools - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
  • Truncation - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
  • User - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse.
  • Usage - Count of Prompt Tokens, Completion Tokens & Total Tokens.
  • Action Status - An object with the following fields:
    • Code - Returns 0 if success and error code if failure occurs.
    • Message - 'Success' if the whole request succeeds or respective error message if a failure occurs.

Error Messages:

  • Invalid Authentication
  • Incorrect API key provided
  • You must be a member of an organization to use the API
  • Rate limit reached for requests
  • You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details
  • The engine is currently overloaded, please try again later
  • The server had an error while processing your request

sys_hub_flow_snapshot.description:
Creates a model response.

Inputs:

  • Model - Model ID used to generate the response.
  • Input - Text, image, or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response.
  • Include - Specify additional output data to include in the model response.
  • Instructions - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
  • Max Output Tokens - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
  • Metadata - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
  • Parallel Tool Calls - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
  • Previous Response ID - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
  • Reasoning - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
    • Effort - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high.
    • Generate Summary - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.
  • Store - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API.
  • Temperature - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
  • Top P - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
  • Send JSON Response - Set to true to enable JSON mode.
  • Response Format - Configuration options for a response from the model as a structured JSON data.
  • Tool Choice - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
  • Tools - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
  • Truncation - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
  • User - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse.

Outputs:

  • Output - An array of content items generated by the model.
  • ID - Unique Id for this response.
  • Object - Details of the API used for the request.
  • Created At - Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when this Response was created.
  • Model - Details of the model used for the request.
  • Status - The status of the response generation. One of completed, failed, in_progress, or incomplete.
  • Incomplete Details - Details about why the response is incomplete.
  • Instructions - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
  • Max Output Tokens - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
  • Metadata - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
  • Parallel Tool Calls - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
  • Previous Response ID - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
  • Reasoning - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
    • Effort - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high.
    • Generate Summary - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.
  • Store - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API.
  • Temperature - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
  • Top P - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
  • Text - Configuration options for a text response from the model. Can be plain text or structured JSON data.
  • Tool Choice - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
  • Tools - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
  • Truncation - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
  • User - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse.
  • Usage - Count of Prompt Tokens, Completion Tokens & Total Tokens.
  • Action Status - An object with the following fields:
    • Code - Returns 0 if success and error code if failure occurs.
    • Message - 'Success' if the whole request succeeds or respective error message if a failure occurs.

Error Messages:

  • Invalid Authentication
  • Incorrect API key provided
  • You must be a member of an organization to use the API
  • Rate limit reached for requests
  • You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details
  • The engine is currently overloaded, please try again later
  • The server had an error while processing your request

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update sys_domain="global" table="sys_hub_flow"><sys_hub_flow action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><access>public</access><acls/><active>false</active><allow_high_security_roles>false</allow_high_security_roles><annotation/><attributes>browserActivatedIn=firefox,integrationActivatedIn=standalone,labelCacheCleanUpExecuted=true,timeFromCreateToActivate=24790593000,viewActivatedIn=naturalLanguage</attributes><authored_on_release_version>26000</authored_on_release_version><callable_by_client_api>false</callable_by_client_api><category display_value="Responses Management">d691dfd9376022103f0265f734924b7a</category><copied_from/><copied_from_name/><description><p>Creates a model response. </p>
<p>
    <b>Inputs:</b>
</p>
<ul>
    <li>
        <strong>Model</strong> - Model ID used to generate the response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Input</strong> - Text, image, or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Include</strong> - Specify additional output data to include in the model response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Instructions</strong> - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Max Output Tokens</strong> - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Metadata</strong> - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Parallel Tool Calls</strong> - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Previous Response ID</strong> - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Reasoning</strong> - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
        <ul>
            <li> <strong>Effort</strong> - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high. </li>
            <li> <strong>Generate Summary</strong> - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li> <strong>Store</strong> - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API. </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Temperature</strong> - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8
        will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Top P</strong> - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where
        the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens
        comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Send JSON Response</strong> - Set to true to enable JSON mode.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Response Format</strong> - Configuration options for a response from the model as a structured JSON data.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tool Choice</strong> - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tools</strong> - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Truncation</strong> - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>User</strong> - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
        monitor and detect abuse.
    </li>
</ul>
<p>
    <b>Outputs:</b>
</p>
<ul>
  <li>
        <strong>Output</strong> - An array of content items generated by the model.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>ID</strong> - Unique Id for this response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Object</strong> - Details of the API used for the request.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Created At</strong> - Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when this Response was created.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Model</strong> - Details of the model used for the request.
    </li>
  <li>
        <strong>Status</strong> - The status of the response generation. One of completed, failed, in_progress, or incomplete.
    </li>
  <li>
        <strong>Incomplete Details</strong> - Details about why the response is incomplete.
    </li>
  <li>
        <strong>Instructions</strong> - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Max Output Tokens</strong> - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Metadata</strong> - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Parallel Tool Calls</strong> - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Previous Response ID</strong> - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Reasoning</strong> - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
        <ul>
            <li> <strong>Effort</strong> - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high. </li>
            <li> <strong>Generate Summary</strong> - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li> <strong>Store</strong> - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API. </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Temperature</strong> - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8
        will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Top P</strong> - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where
        the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens
        comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Text</strong> - Configuration options for a text response from the model. Can be plain text or structured JSON data.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tool Choice</strong> - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tools</strong> - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Truncation</strong> - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>User</strong> - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
        monitor and detect abuse.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Usage</strong> - Count of Prompt Tokens, Completion Tokens & Total Tokens.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Action Status</strong> - An object with the following fields:
        <ul>
            <li>
                <strong>Code</strong> - Returns 0 if success and error code if failure occurs.
            </li>
            <li>
                <strong>Message</strong> - 'Success' if the whole request succeeds or respective error message
                if a failure occurs.
            </li>
        </ul>
    </li>
</ul>

<p>
    <b>Error Messages:</b>
</p>
<ul>
    <li>Invalid Authentication</li>
    <li>Incorrect API key provided</li>
    <li>You must be a member of an organization to use the API</li>
    <li>Rate limit reached for requests</li>
    <li>You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details</li>
    <li>The engine is currently overloaded, please try again later</li>
    <li>The server had an error while processing your request</li>
</ul></description><display_name_after_preview/><flow_priority>MEDIUM</flow_priority><generation_source/><internal_name>create_response_wrapper</internal_name><label_cache>[{"name":"subflow.request_metadata","label":"Input➛Request display_value="Responses Management">d691dfd9376022103f0265f734924b7a</category><copied_from/><copied_from_name/><description><p>Creates a model response. </p>
<p>
    <b>Inputs:</b>
</p>
<ul>
    <li>
        <strong>Model</strong> - Model ID used to generate the response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Input</strong> - Text, image, or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Include</strong> - Specify additional output data to include in the model response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Instructions</strong> - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Max Output Tokens</strong> - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Metadata</strong> - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Parallel Tool Calls</strong> - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Previous Response ID</strong> - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Reasoning</strong> - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
        <ul>
            <li> <strong>Effort</strong> - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high. </li>
            <li> <strong>Generate Summary</strong> - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li> <strong>Store</strong> - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API. </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Temperature</strong> - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8
        will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Top P</strong> - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where
        the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens
        comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Send JSON Response</strong> - Set to true to enable JSON mode.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Response Format</strong> - Configuration options for a response from the model as a structured JSON data.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tool Choice</strong> - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tools</strong> - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Truncation</strong> - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>User</strong> - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
        monitor and detect abuse.
    </li>
</ul>
<p>
    <b>Outputs:</b>
</p>
<ul>
  <li>
        <strong>Output</strong> - An array of content items generated by the model.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>ID</strong> - Unique Id for this response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Object</strong> - Details of the API used for the request.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Created At</strong> - Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when this Response was created.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Model</strong> - Details of the model used for the request.
    </li>
  <li>
        <strong>Status</strong> - The status of the response generation. One of completed, failed, in_progress, or incomplete.
    </li>
  <li>
        <strong>Incomplete Details</strong> - Details about why the response is incomplete.
    </li>
  <li>
        <strong>Instructions</strong> - Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Max Output Tokens</strong> - An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Metadata</strong> - Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Parallel Tool Calls</strong> - Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Previous Response ID</strong> - The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to create multi-turn conversations.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Reasoning</strong> - An object with the following fields to configure reasoning models.
        <ul>
            <li> <strong>Effort</strong> - Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are low, medium, and high. </li>
            <li> <strong>Generate Summary</strong> - A summary of the reasoning performed by the model. This can be useful for debugging and understanding the model's reasoning process. One of concise or detailed.</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li> <strong>Store</strong> - Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API. </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Temperature</strong> - The sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8
        will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Top P</strong> - An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where
        the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens
        comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Text</strong> - Configuration options for a text response from the model. Can be plain text or structured JSON data.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tool Choice</strong> - How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Tools</strong> - An array of tools the model may call while generating a response.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Truncation</strong> - The truncation strategy to use for the model response. Supported values are: auto, disabled (default).
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>User</strong> - A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
        monitor and detect abuse.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Usage</strong> - Count of Prompt Tokens, Completion Tokens & Total Tokens.
    </li>
    <li>
        <strong>Action Status</strong> - An object with the following fields:
        <ul>
            <li>
                <strong>Code</strong> - Returns 0 if success and error code if failure occurs.
            </li>
            <li>
                <strong>Message</strong> - 'Success' if the whole request succeeds or respective error message
                if a failure occurs.
            </li>
        </ul>
    </li>
</ul>
